test_title: Delhi Police Constable (Executive) 2023 - GK/CA (Held on: 30 Nov, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: gk
question:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding the tribal Festival Medaram Jathara?

A. This is the largest tribal festival of India.

B. This festival is celebrated by the Koya community of Telangana.

C. This festival is celebrated once in two years in the month of 'Magha' (February) on the full moon day.
solution:
The correct answer is __**A, B, and C**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Medaram Jathara** is considered the **largest tribal festival in India**.
 
• This festival is celebrated by the **Koya tribal community**, which is predominantly found in **Telangana**.
 
• The festival honors **Sammakka and Saralamma**, two tribal women who are worshipped as goddesses.
 
• It is celebrated **once every two years** during the month of **Magha (February)** on the **full moon day**.
 
• Medaram Jathara is held at **Medaram village**, located in the **Mulugu district** of Telangana.
 
• It attracts a large number of devotees, making it one of the most significant religious and tribal gatherings in India.
 
• The event is conducted in harmony with the region's **tribal traditions** and practices, without excessive modern interference.
 
• The Government of Telangana provides logistical support to ensure smooth conduct of the festival.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Koya Community**__

 __
 
• The **Koya** are a tribal community primarily found in the **forest areas** of Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, and Chhattisgarh.
 
• They traditionally practice **shifting cultivation** and are known for their rich **cultural heritage**.
 
• The Koya people venerate Sammakka and Saralamma as their **ancestral deities**.
 
 
 
• **Sammakka and Saralamma**__
 
 
• Sammakka and Saralamma were two **tribal women warriors** who fought against the **Kakatiya rulers** in defense of their community.
 
• They are worshipped as deities for their **bravery and sacrifice**.
 
• Their story is integral to the **Medaram Jathara** and reflects the tribal community's connection to nature and resistance to external oppression.
